svg.title: Bytes per hop for one TraceQL search, evaluated after transport against lowered into SQL
svg.desc: The query { .service.namespace = "prod" } | max(duration) > 1s with limit 20 over a five-day window, on corpus C1. Evaluated today it costs 1,128 sequential round trips between pulsus-server and ClickHouse, moving 77,572,021 result bytes of which 11,340 bytes reach the client. Lowered it costs 4 round trips moving 212,986 result bytes in total, across all four statements: the compiled generator, the window-bounded hydration read, the membership read and the winners' root read. The last stays residual in every chain because the root summary is read trace-wide with no time predicate — residual meaning it cannot join the first statement, not that our own process performs it: it is the plan's second SQL part. The client hop is unchanged. The pulsus-server to ClickHouse hop and the client hop are metered in a multi-zone deployment; the parts-to-ClickHouse hop is local disk and is not. Database peak memory rises from 167,629,277 to 190,817,746 bytes, both of them the phase-1 generator's. Every figure in this drawing is a total over docs/benchmarks/data/traces-lowering-92.json, which holds one system.query_log row per statement, and is the same total query-lowering.md 9.2 and 9.2b state.
svg.text: limit=20, 5-day window, 10,000,000-span corpus C1. One system.query_log row per statement, 1,132 of them, retained.
Evaluated after transport (today) — 1,128 sequential round trips
1 candidate generator + 563 x (hydration + membership) + 1 winners' root read
Every one of the 563 membership reads selected 1,105 granules and read 9,052,160 rows. That is stated over all 563, not most of them:
the artefact holds one row per statement, so the per-read unit and the phase total are two readings of the same evidence (query-lowering.md 9.2).
Lowered into SQL — 4 round trips: a plan of two SQL parts, the second seeded by the first's 20 trace ids (Emit is Never)
Two SQL parts, four statements. The hydration and membership reads survive lowering, and the root summary is
trace-wide and unwindowed, so Emit is Never — Never means a link cannot join part 0, not that no statement serves it.
Metered hop 364x fewer bytes · 282x fewer round trips · 290x fewer rows read · 290x fewer granules
Both sides count the whole request, all four lowered statements included, so the ratios compare like with like.
Database peak memory HIGHER — 167,629,277 B against 190,817,746 B, a ratio of 1.14x computed from those two figures,
both of them the phase-1 generator's — and spending database memory to move fewer bytes is the direction the cost
† moves with part layout (Compact against Wide), and is the one column that is not bit-reproducible between runs. Granules, rows, decoded bytes and result bytes are — measured twice, see 9.2.
